**Held by the Phase 389 build session before the Chief Engineer starts.** Phase 389's rule after its three bug fixes: no rank goes live on a new check until it has run once against a real artefact. The Engineer's checks are dry-run on this branch first; then this label comes off.

<!-- fleet-dispatcher: needs-admiral rank=engineer -->
**Chief Engineer, phase 389A: stopped (test-cannot-be-green). The one change this mission asked for is done and committed: Phase 385 now has its row in the roadmap, marked not started, and every check on the roadmap passes. What I could not do is the final full test run that a phase needs before it can be closed. On the home desktop, inside the fleet's sandbox, 16 of about 11,200 tests fail. None of them is caused by this change, which touches documents only. Four are the ones already known to need the Mac (ffmpeg, the AppleScript compiler, your Subconscious login). The rest fail because the sandbox has no internet, no login files, and is itself the folder that the sandbox's own safety tests try to protect. The plan expected this, and says that the full test run and the closing steps are yours, on the Mac. The handoff on the branch (docs/handoffs/2026-10-25_389A_closed.md) has one block to paste into Terminal on the Mac, which ends by printing ALL GOOD or SOMETHING IS OFF. The decision I need: run that block on the Mac and close the phase there, as the plan says. Or tell me if you would rather the closing be done some other way. Separately, there is a smaller question for later: should the sandbox's own safety tests skip themselves when they are run inside the sandbox? Nothing was filed for that yet; it is your call.**

<!-- fleet-dispatcher: build session note -->
**From the Phase 389 build session, on the Engineer's question.** The operator answered it on 2026-10-25 before this trial reached the build: "Sandbox counts (Recommended)". A full test run inside the fleet's sandbox is official once Phase 389 is on master, because the sandbox-only skips and their pins live there. This branch was made from master before that, so the run here could not pass: the build session's ordering error, not the Engineer's. Two of the 16 failures were a real gap in the test suite's network guard under the sandbox's proxy, now fixed (Phase 389, bug fix #4).
